item.text:
The context limit is model-dependent. For the currently documented models, it is generally 256k tokens—for example, Mistral Small 4 and Mistral Large 3 both specify a 256k context window. Older models such as Mistral Medium 3.1 and Codestral specify 128k. Requests exceeding the model’s window should return HTTP 400. [Mistral model limits](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations)

A 308 kB PDF should not cost 321,774 tokens merely because it is Base64. In the documented format, Base64 is placed in a `data:application/pdf;base64,...` `document_url`; Mistral then runs OCR and supplies the extracted document to the language model. [Document QnA](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/document-processing/document_qna)

The likely explanation is that the PDF’s page was rasterized and passed through the multimodal document pipeline. Image inputs are represented as special vision-token sequences, whose size depends mainly on rendered resolution—not compressed PDF file size. A single dense/high-resolution page can therefore expand to hundreds of thousands of prompt tokens, explaining both the 321,774-token count and the ~400-second latency. Mistral’s image-tokenization documentation confirms that images are converted into sequences of special tokens. [Mistral image inputs](https://mistralai.github.io/mistral-common/usage/images/)

Also check that the request did not accidentally put the Base64 string in a normal text field or enable image-inclusive OCR output; use a proper `document_url` data URI and avoid unnecessary embedded image data.
